explainer_content.short_definition: The 1970s album-rock backbone: canonical LPs, FM-radio standards, guitar bands, and songs that became shared rock memory.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Classic rock is an afterlife as much as an era. Led Zeppelin, Pink Floyd, Fleetwood Mac, Eagles, Creedence, Queen, and related artists were made durable through albums, touring, radio repetition, and later canon-building.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It became the default rock reference library for several generations: riffs, album covers, long songs, stadium scale, road-trip radio, and deep-cut familiarity.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: The lane is broad but not random; its center is the album-rock listening habit, where songs and LPs become durable objects together.
what_to_listen_for: Guitar riffs that work as public memory
Studio craft large enough for arena or headphones
Deep cuts that sound familiar from radio
A balance of virtuosity and singalong access
